item.title:
Sunday, July 26, 2026 - Topic: On this week’s show, Radio Intifada’s co-hosts Rana Sharif and David Lloyd speak with Dr. Hanine Shehadeh about a project, based at the American University in Beirut, to archive every record of the Israeli genocide in Gaza, from the videos of atrocities filmed and posted by Palestinians on social media to details of the lives and hoped-for futures of the–at least–75,000 Gazans martyred in Israel’s ongoing genocide that has now surpassed the 1000 day mark. We then turn to Professor Hannah Appel, an organizer with UC Move Your Money, a divestment campaign aimed at getting UC faculty to move their UC retirement savings from investments linked to Israeli state violence and instead allocate funds to the UC Social Equity Fund.
On the heels of the conclusion of the world cup, in our final segment we celebrate the survival and the ongoing life of Palestinians in Gaza through the story of Palestinian football star Mohammed Balah, whose career as the "Ronaldo of Gaza" was nearly cut short by Israel’s genocide and whose family, still trapped in Gaza, continue to face bombardment, hunger, and displacement. We talk with Anne Habiby, co-author with Mohammed Balah of Daring to Hope: Witness from Gaza, a new book that tells Mohammed’s story of displacement, injury, and determination to survive and play on in the name of Gaza.
